== Missing data ==

* No 1999 Worlds player packet was found. Category One Games posted the 1998 packet (Kendrick Summers letterhead, 20 November 1998) at blog.categoryonegames.com/star-wars-worlds-1998/; that post and PDF hunt for 1999 returned empty. Decipher's live swworldchamp pages (finalists, Round of 12, SW.03, Lalumiere wraps) are the surviving official record.
* ''Star Wars Insider'' coverage of 1999 Worlds is absent from the dested issues (1998 used Insider #43).
* Decipher posted 100×100 GIF portraits on final12.html; too small to dest.
* Remaining Saturday/Friday DecipherCon photo captions were not dested beyond sat14 (Gary Carman).
* Martin Akesson wrote that he won Thursday Progressive Sealed against Aldrin Long. [[DecipherCon 1999 Progressive Sealed Deck]] still has two differing SW22 sheets and a blank winner; that claim is not dested here.
* Day 1 places outside the twelve and Lush's 28th are not on an official score sheet.

== Possibly faulty data ==

* Hometowns and spellings follow Decipher finalists.html (ratings as of 3 October 1999). Conflicts left off the article:
** [[Gary Carman]]: Birmingham (finalists/final12) vs Bristol (TheForce.Net 14 November 1999; Lalumiere Saturday; RFD 38). TFN spelled "Garry Carmen"; Lalumiere spelled "Garry Carman".
** [[Clint Hays]]: Juliet, Tennessee (1999 list) vs Mt. Juliet (1998 packet).
** [[Steven Lewis]]: Nashville (finalists) vs Franklin (final12).
** [[Yannick Lapointe]]: Ottawa, Ontario (finalists) vs Laval, Quebec (final12).
** [[Paul Todd Feldman]]: Mountain View (finalists) vs Turlock, California (final12).
** [[Jason Kilby]]: Portland (finalists) vs Aloha, Oregon (final12).
** [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] spelled Bastien on final12.
* Akesson report Day 1 total 10 (+46); official prelims 10 (45). Article uses official.
* Akesson called [[Gregory Reid]] a 1996 and 1997 finalist; those years are not dested on Reid's stub without the packets.

== Marginal cuts ==

* Wikipedia World Champions table (32 Round-1 participants, Virginia Beach) is tertiary to finalists.html.
* Akesson Progressive Sealed narrative (see Missing data).
* Lush game-by-game (Nardulli Dantooine Base Operations, Atkin Hidden Base inserts, Fred TIE Advanced, Jones Intruder Missiles on the Executor). Finish 28th is dested.

== Invitee numbers, Day 1 decks, Final Confrontation (2026-10-24) ==

Wild Card stays a section of the Worlds hub. Dest titles stay [[1999 Decipher World Championship]] with Stage Wild Card. [[1999 Decipher World Championship Scott Lingrell Yavin IVCheese]] now has Stage Wild Card and Finish 8–2 (Wild Card). Analog is 2000 Day 1, which is also a section.

Qualifiers # numbers the 32 invitees. [[Matt Potter]] is 1 as the 1998 World Champion. Opens, Invitationals, and regionals then follow Decipher finalists.html. Wild Card is last: [[John Arendt]] 31, [[James Lafferty]] 32. Regional dates are unpublished, so that order is not by event date. The old Finish column mixed Day 1 and Day 2 places and is gone.

Day 1 now has Place, Prelims, Dark, and Light. Official twelve plus Lush 28th. Also [[Maarten Logghe]], [[Markus Wüst]], and Lush pairing names [[Piergiulio Nardulli]], [[Clayton Atkin]], [[Brian Fred]], [[Aldrin Long]]. [[Gregory Reid]] and [[Stuart Jones]] already have prelim scores. Remaining Day 1 places are unpublished.

Day 1 dests: Lafferty (Deck Designs: he brought the pair to the prelims; Lush game 4 ISB). Akesson Ralltiir Operations (Lush game 2). Hays and Winkelhaus Worlds lists; no rebuild is sourced. Logghe, Wuest, and Lush Light. Carman and Lewis dests sit in Final Confrontation. Carman rebuilt overnight after Day 1.

Results is the championship 12 after the Final Confrontation, Finish and Player only. Decks used on Friday sit in Day 1. Championship dests sit in Final Confrontation.

Final Confrontation sits after Day 2.
